== Overview ==

There are approximately 25,000 Suwa Shrines throughout Japan, all having {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}} in Nagano Prefecture as their head shrine. Suwa Faith revolves around the veneration of {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|it|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata}}, the main deity, and his consort {{ill|Yasakatome|ja|八坂刀売神|simple|Yasakatome|zh|八坂刀賣神|qid=Q9150392|lt=Yasakatome no Kami}}. Together, they are referred to as the "Suwa Deities" (諏訪大神). When Suwa Grand Shrine's deities are transferred to other Suwa Shrines, their divine spirits are believed to reside within a ritual {{ill|Nagi Kama|ja|薙鎌|qid=Q11622229}}, which becomes the sacred object of the shrine.

Suwa Grand Shrine conducts the renowned {{ill|Onbashira|es|Onbashira|fr|Onbashira|ja|御柱祭|ru|Омбасира|vi|Onbashira|qid=Q3698846|lt=Onbashira Festival}}, held every six years. Many Suwa Shrines across the country host similar festivals. Additionally, rituals like the spring {{ill|Ontōsai|ja|御頭祭}} and {{ill|Misayama Festival|ja|御射山祭}}, a traditional hunting ceremony in late August, are celebrated at various Suwa Shrines.
